record.original_question: Let G be a cubic planar graph and let L be a 3-list-assignment on G. Is it always possible to choose three pairwise-disjoint proper L-colorings, that is, three proper colorings from the given vertex lists such that each vertex receives three different colors across the three colorings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a cubic planar graph (a planar graph in which every vertex has degree exactly 3). A list-assignment on $G$ is a function $L$ that assigns to each vertex $v \in V(G)$ a set $L(v)$ of permissible colors; it is a 3-list-assignment if $|L(v)| = 3$ for every $v$. An $L$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c: V(G) \to \mathbb{N}$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v$; it is proper if $c(u) \neq c(v)$ whenever $u$ and $v$ are adjacent. Two $L$-colorings $c_i, c_j$ are called disjoint if $c_i(u) \neq c_j(u)$ for every vertex $u \in V(G)$.

Question: For every cubic planar graph $G$ and every 3-list-assignment $L$ on $G$, do there always exist three pairwise-disjoint proper $L$-colorings of $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in workshop problem collections on cycles and colorings. Related work (Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, Kang and others on "disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs") shows that for general planar graphs with 3-list-assignments three disjoint proper L-colorings cannot always be guaranteed, but the cubic planar case remains a posed open problem; no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies list packing number of planar graphs; for girth 3 planar graphs three disjoint L-colorings cannot be guaranteed in general, while results improve at higher girth.
status_evidence.claim: The triple-packing question for 3-list-assignments is studied for planar graphs but not resolved for the cubic planar case.

status_evidence.title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems presented by participants, including questions on disjoint proper L-colorings of cubic planar graphs with 3-list-assignments.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an open problem in a workshop problem collection.
